newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU employers sees decline in competitiveness.
newsitem.headline: EU employers sees decline in competitiveness.

text.p: The European employers' group UNICE said on Thursday competitiveness continued to decline and it was time to study whether the functioning of the labour market itself was a major cause behind Europe's high unemployment rate.

UNICE, which groups industry and employers' federations from 25 European countries, welcomed the Commission's Communication on "Benchmarking the Competitiveness of European Industry" which was published on October 9.
Benchmarking is seen as a tool to boost the competitive power of Europe's industry, which is lagging behind the performance in both the United States and Japan.

"(The communication) is strong proof that the Commission, and especially Industrial Affairs Commissioner Martin Bangemann, have heard and understood the concerns of companies faced with the continuing decline of European competitiveness and are prepared to act to reverse the trend," UNICE President Francois Perigot said in a press release.
He said Europe suffers from low rates of net job creation and employment.
"It is high time to look more deeply into this phenomenon and see to what extent the functioning of the labour market itself can be considered a major cause," Perigot said.
He said early publication of a Commission report on the "Competitiveness of European Industry", on which the Commission Communication was based, would stimulate the implementation of any actions.
